spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:**
[GAP-1: REVIEW The] whole of the lust to appropriate what belongs to divine good is this primordial proprium — the original self-derived will — that arose in the states of falsity from evil.

**¶2:**
In this lust to appropriate, which [GAP-2: ...] within it, the Divine Good descending into combat [GAP-3: ...] its persuasive falsity [GAP-4: ...] its active working of evil. The external truths that clothed the Divine Good were [GAP-5: ...] — the falsity from evil severed and stripped them away; [GAP-6: ...]

**¶3:**
It lusted to possess the first manifestation of the Divine Wisdom sent forth, which the Lord as Divine Truth displayed before it from the celestial states above, in the form of divine order which it perceived outwardly. From this perception, evil fashioned a counterfeit likeness and an imitation form within what is merely corporeal and natural, impressing the semblance of that divine form upon its own proprium — a thing generated entirely from its own self-derived will.

**¶4:**
A [th]ird time it lusted to appropriate what belonged to Adam — the Most Ancient Church, the celestial human in its earliest state. Evil seized a living faculty from that church, and brought forth from it something derived from the [GAP-7: REVIEW innermost natural proprium of] the celestial human's [GAP-8: REVIEW self-derived will] — appropriating the very proprium that had little life of its own, and generating from it a counterfeit form of the will separated from celestial good.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
In this envy that [existed] in it, the First Man [swallowed] its poiso[n and] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [seized and] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]

It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
[The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].

fills.explanation: The definite article "The" naturally opens the introductory definition "The entirety of envy is this first nature," and the spiritual reading confirms this phrasing.
The spiritual reading indicates envy dwelling/existing "within it" (the dark nature), and "existed" is the standard Kephalaia verb for a quality subsisting within a substance.

In the Manichaean cosmogony the First Man's sons swallowed the poison of the archons as part of the cosmic combat strategy; the spiritual reading confirms the Divine Good "descending into combat" took on the persuasive falsity of darkness.
The partial word completes "poison" and the conjunction "and" connects it to "its evil-doing," matching the spiritual reading's pairing of persuasive falsity and active working of evil.

The spiritual reading indicates the external truths (garments) were captured by evil before being severed and stripped; "seized" provides the correct sequential logic preceding "it cut them and drew them."

The editor's "rib of" is confirmed: in Swedenborg the rib (bone) signifies the proprium — the self-derived will with little life — which is exactly what the spiritual reading identifies as the "innermost natural proprium" from which evil generated a counterfeit form.

The editor's "flesh" is confirmed: in Swedenborg "flesh" corresponds to the voluntary proprium (self-derived will, AC 148), and the spiritual reading identifies this position as "self-derived will" — the exact correspondential match.
